abstract: This paper develops a new measure of occupational exposure to AI and examines labor market impacts for highly exposed workers since late 2022. The authors find no systematic increase in unemployment for workers in AI-exposed occupations, but identify suggestive evidence that hiring of younger workers has slowed in these exposed occupations, indicating potential differential impacts across age groups.
keyFindings: No systematic increase in unemployment for highly exposed workers since late 2022, contrary to some automation displacement concerns.
Suggestive evidence that hiring of younger workers has slowed in occupations with high AI exposure.
Study develops a new measure of occupational AI exposure to assess labor market vulnerability.
Differential labor market impacts appear to exist across demographic groups, particularly by age.
